message:
sara: Heads up — customer 'Fjord Labs' reports Console started returning 403s right after we renamed their org. API calls with service tokens succeed but UI actions (Invite, Project settings) fail with 'permission denied'. Anyone seen this pattern?

jonathan: Any idea if it's scoped to a subset of users or all members? SSO vs API keys? :thinking:

sara: Only SSO-authenticated users. Service accounts and direct API keys continue to work. They renamed the org about ~1h ago. Affected users can still login via SSO, land in the Console, but clicking certain actions returns a 403 overlay.

alex: Can you paste a failing request/response and the user's JWT (redacted)? Also which endpoint is 403ing (ui call vs backend /orgs API)?

sara: Pasting sanitized logs below. Customer repro: login -> go to org settings -> click 'Members' -> UI fetch to /api/orgs/9a1b/members returns 403.

```
Request: GET /api/orgs/9a1b/members
Response: 403 {"error":"permission denied"}
User JWT claims (sanitized):
{
  "sub":"user:U123",
  "email":"user@fjord.example",
  "auth_method":"sso",
  "scopes":["console:view","project:read"],
  "roles":["member"],
  "org_id":"9a1b",
  "iat": 1610000000
}
```

ida: Interesting — JWT shows scopes but not an explicit 'org:admin' or 'role:admin' claim. Do they have a mapping from IdP groups -> console roles that might have been invalidated by the rename? Could be SCIM group IDs vs group names mismatch.

sara: They said group names didn't change, but our audit shows the IdP sent SCIM patch for the org rename and some group-member links returned 404 from the IdP side during the window. Might be a partial sync where members persisted in our DB but role bindings didn't get re-applied.

jonathan: Two quick diagnostics:
1) Check internal role-propagation logs for org 9a1b (job runner status)
2) Inspect the identity sync events for SCIM errors around the rename timestamp

alex: I triggered a manual resync for the org via the internal endpoint and also kicked off role propagation. Command I ran (internal-only):

```
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOOL_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal.console.redwood/api/v1/orgs/9a1b/identity/resync"

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOOL_TOKEN" \
  "https://internal.console.redwood/api/v1/orgs/9a1b/roles/propagate"
```

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-20216 created and linked to thread. Notifying CSM and infra oncall. :white_check_mark:

ida: I watched the role propagation job run. It found ~22 member bindings that were missing role assignments and wrote them back. No fatal errors, just a race where SCIM retries returned 409/404 and left inconsistent state.

sara: Customer confirmed at 06:47 UTC that members can now see Project settings and invites; 403s gone for previously affected users. They had to fully sign out and sign back in once we applied the propagation fix.

jonathan: Root cause hypothesis: org rename triggered SCIM patches; some group membership patches failed transiently, leaving our internal role mapping stale. Console checks role bindings from the role table at request time, so stale bindings produced 403 despite valid SSO session.

alex: Short-term mitigation: when org rename events occur we should kick an immediate identity resync + role propagation, and surface a retryable error that suggests user sign-out/sign-in. Longer-term: make SCIM apply idempotent reconciliation for name/ID drift and add a small delay window that queues retries for failed group patches.

ida: Follow-up actions logged:
- Run daily audit job to detect orgs with recent renames and missing role assignments (created #INFRA-789)
- Add alert on propagation job failure rate (created #SRE-452)
- Update support runbook: recommend forced resync + user sign-out for similar incidents (PR in docs repo)

sara: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer with the remediation steps and close the ticket once they confirm no recurrence. If they see it again we'll escalate to IdP vendor and collect SCIM logs. :wave:
